dag_id_prefix_means: A job's Airflow DAG id is this prefix and its id. orchestration/dags/job_specs.py names the DAGs with it, and foundation-api (GET /data-catalog/v1/scheduled-jobs, root ADR-0165) finds each job's run records in the data catalog under the flow its DAG reports as.
description: Every scheduled data job (root ADR-0118, ADR-0122). What a job runs, as whom, with which environment and time limit is its systemd service in infra/systemd and nowhere else. This list adds when it runs, its resource pool, the pipeline-graph edges it carries out (its lineage, read from docs/catalog/pipeline-graph.v1.json) and whether Airflow runs it yet. A job that checks data rather than moving it names no edges and sets reads_data_contracts: its inputs are the tables the data contracts cover.

spark.description: The host's scheduled heavy work (root ADR-0138): FLOOR and lineage take all three slots (20g Spark) and run alone; a map-edit fold takes two, so the folds never overlap (their Spark runs share one init container name); the by-PNU bake takes one, so one fold can run beside it; the panel Gold rebuild and each hub Silver refresh lane take all three (20g Spark) and run alone. The host memory guard checks every combination these slots allow.

pools_means: Every Airflow pool a job may name, besides Airflow's own default_pool, with its slot count; a job takes pool_slots of them (1 when absent). scripts/deploy/airflow-runtime.sh creates exactly these. orchestration/dags/job_specs.py refuses a job naming any other pool, a pool_slots above the pool's slots, and a job that could hold slots another job needs for longer than STARVATION_CYCLES runs of that job. scripts/guard/every-container-has-a-memory-cap.sh adds up the memory of every set of jobs the slots let run together (root ADR-0138). compose.orchestration.yml's AIRFLOW__CORE__PARALLELISM is at least the slots here plus one, so a default_pool job always has a slot (orchestration/tests/test_job_specs.py). A job's priority_weight decides which waiting job Airflow starts first when slots free (FLOOR and lineage above the folds, the folds above the Silver refresh lanes, the lanes above the Gold rebuild, the Gold rebuild above the bake). retries (1 when absent) is how often Airflow runs it again after a failure. A takes_turns job starts at most once between scheduled starts of every job in its pool that cannot run beside it: scripts/ops/start-scheduled-job.sh keeps the starts and defers it, so a multi-day bake cannot keep FLOOR and lineage waiting run after run.
enabled_means: Airflow starts the job's service on the schedule here; its systemd timer is gone from infra/systemd and the release retires it from the host (ADR-0122 §4). A job runs in exactly one of the two places.
started_by_means: What starts a job (root ADR-0171). `schedule`: Airflow starts it at its schedule. `inputs`: Airflow starts it as soon as a run of another job reports that it changed one of the job's inputs (the pipeline-graph nodes its edges start from), and at its schedule as well, the fallback for what no event announces: a hand load, a run outside Airflow, a run while its DAG was paused, a failed or deferred run. Each input and output is an Airflow asset named by its data catalog dataset; which job feeds which is read from the edges here, never written down a second time. A run says whether it changed its outputs with a last line `foundation-job-outcome changed|unchanged`; only `unchanged` withholds its output events, so a job that does not say counts as changed. orchestration/dags/job_specs.py refuses an `inputs` job no listed job feeds, an enabled one whose feeders are all off, one that writes its own input, and jobs that start each other in a circle.

Parcel lineage stewardship cycle: fold steward decisions, rebuild and load the review queue (root ADR-0115). First it loads any pending 필지고유번호변동연혁 handoff into silver.parcel_number_change_history (root ADR-0144 §4), then loads and pairs any pending legal-dong code handoff (root ADR-0143), reading the official links of the pairing window once that table holds rows: the snapshot into reference.legal_dong_code_snapshot, the changes into reference.legal_dong_code_change (the one record of region code changes, root ADR-0145), and the crosswalk projection the hub exports read, a view of that table; a failure there fails the run before lineage starts.

Legal-dong code changes from code.go.kr (root ADR-0143, ADR-0144), the collection half: land the full table (codes, parents, created and abolished dates) in Bronze (requests at least 15 seconds apart; the change-notice board is not a source), refuse a response whose shape changed or a table that shrank past the contract's bounds, record when the table was last confirmed, and, only when the table's rows changed, write a pending-load handoff. No Spark: lineage_stewardship loads and pairs the handoff under its spark slots before its own steps.

VWorld cadastral parcel editions (연속지적도, MK/30563; root ADR-0148): check the provider's newest edition against the source contract (vworld-parcel-source-objects.json); when it is new, collect its directly downloadable files into Bronze, measure each ZIP's members by ranged read, and propose the contract entry. No Spark: the Silver load runs from a release whose contract holds the edition (runbook vworld-parcel-editions.md). Exit 3 means an edition awaits the contract, not a fault: the job posts 'new edition waiting for contract entry' itself, and is not retried (a retry would only download and propose the same edition again).
jobs.disabled_reason: New. Off until one supervised run on the data host (runbook vworld-parcel-editions.md, 'Turning it on') has answered 'held' for the edition the contract holds; switching it on is a separate deploy step (ADR-0122 §4).

jobs.description: Rebuild gold.parcel_panel, then gold.building_panel, with their existing Spark producers when a Silver input changed rows since the snapshots the current Gold was built from; otherwise nothing (root ADR-0139). Each rebuild pins its inputs, refuses before writing a Gold that fails its checks or loses more rows than infra/lakehouse/contracts/gold-panel-rebuild.contract.json allows, and commits one new snapshot recording its pins. Started when a run of a job that writes one of those Silver inputs changed it, and at 08:45 as the fallback for hand loads (root ADR-0171); a committed rebuild starts the by-PNU bake, which bakes a Gold snapshot it does not serve yet.

Reflect each new Gold snapshot of gold.parcel_panel, then gold.building_panel, in R2 by-PNU serving (root ADR-0096, ADR-0100, ADR-0141): a row_digest change set (by_pnu_panel_delta.py in the spark-small service, sequential with the export) decides between a create-only patch generation of the changed documents and tombstones, a manifest that only advances the reflected snapshot, and a full new base (forced with a reason, a document schema change, max_patches reached, or the cumulative change ratio exceeded). A patch is published only when its shards wrote exactly its change set; a base only when the shards' exported rows add up to the Gold row count. The lanes run one after the other in one unit: side by side they would not fit the host memory budget (root ADR-0138). Once a lane's manifest carries a section_packs block (root ADR-0147; the parcel lane too, ADR-0160), that lane bakes and publishes section packs instead: the change set goes from the packs' reflected snapshot, a patch writes each section's packs under the generation the lane serves it from, and a full bake is a new generation of every section. Started when a Gold rebuild committed a new snapshot, and at 10:15 as the fallback (root ADR-0171); a turn it defers (takes_turns) is taken at the next start.

started_once_after_deploy_means: The release deploy (scripts/deploy/foundation-deploy.sh, root ADR-0159) starts the job once under the new release, after the switch and before the DAGs are unpaused, and fails the deploy, leaving the DAGs paused, when it does not succeed. It marks the jobs short enough to run inside a deploy; the long Spark jobs are left to their schedule.
capabilities_means: What a job's release can do that another command checks before relying on it. by_pnu_serving_bake's building_section_pack_patches and parcel_section_pack_patches say the bake patches a lane's section packs once its manifest names them (root ADR-0147, ADR-0160); publish-building-by-pnu-section-packs refuses the first pack publish unless the installed release's job declares it, the capability the building gateway contract names (config/r2-connections.contract.json, building_by_pnu_gateway.section_packs.scheduled_bake).
disabled_reason_means: A job may be listed before Airflow runs it: enabled false, no systemd timer, and disabled_reason says why it is off and what turns it on. The host refuses to start a job that is not enabled (scripts/ops/start-scheduled-job.sh), so a listed but disabled job runs nowhere until a deploy switches it on.
serving_surfaces_without_a_job_means: Every pipeline-graph serving surface whose surface_kind is r2_baked_documents or tiles is produced by a job in this list (a job edge ends at it), or is named here with the reason it has none yet. orchestration/tests/test_job_specs.py refuses a baked surface with neither, and an entry here that is stale (the surface has a job, or is not a baked surface).

serving_surfaces_without_a_job.reason: The national parcel tiles are rebaked from the lakehouse (root ADR-0133); that bake's job is registered with the ADR-0133 work, not here. Until then they are baked by hand per docs/runbooks/tiles-object-storage-first-slice.md.
